answers.answer: To govern intercompany lending effectively and avoid sloppy AFR and true-up failures, Lakeshore must implement a structured framework that emphasizes accountability and transparency. The owner of this initiative should be the Global CFO, who will trigger the process by establishing clear guidelines and expectations for intercompany transactions. Evidence of compliance will include a comprehensive promissory-note discipline, which ensures that all intercompany loans are documented and adhere to arms-length principles. Failure modes may arise from inadequate documentation or lack of adherence to established workflows, leading to discrepancies in financial reporting. The next action involves developing a monthly true-up workflow that reconciles intercompany balances and ensures that all parties are aligned on their financial positions. This workflow should be supported by a robust audit trail to facilitate oversight and compliance with regulatory requirements.

Before presenting predictive cash forecasting to the board, Lakeshore must remediate several cash visibility gaps. Key areas include ensuring that the Kyriba platform is fully operational and that all relevant data feeds are accurate and reconciled. The owner of this initiative should be the Treasurer, who will trigger the remediation process by identifying specific gaps in cash visibility. Evidence of progress will include a completed bank connectivity setup, accurate ERP feed quality, and a fully loaded entity hierarchy. Failure modes may include reliance on manual processes or incomplete data, which could lead to inaccurate forecasts. The next action is to establish a timeline for addressing these gaps, ensuring that all stakeholders are informed and engaged in the process.

The board should distinguish between projected, committed, measuring, and realized Kyriba value by establishing clear definitions and metrics for each category. Projected value refers to anticipated benefits based on current plans, while committed value represents formally approved initiatives with allocated resources. Measuring value involves tracking performance against established KPIs, and realized value is the actual financial impact observed post-implementation. The owner of this framework should be the CFO, who will trigger the process by defining these categories and ensuring alignment across the organization. Evidence will include documented value propositions and performance reports. Failure modes may arise from misalignment in definitions or inadequate tracking mechanisms. The next action is to develop a comprehensive reporting framework that captures these distinctions and provides regular updates to the board.

The go/no-go rule for retiring spreadsheet cash-position workflows hinges on the successful implementation of automated cash management systems, such as Kyriba. The owner of this initiative should be the Treasurer, who will trigger the decision by assessing the reliability and accuracy of the new system compared to existing spreadsheet methods. Evidence of readiness will include successful testing of the new system, user adoption rates, and reconciliation accuracy. Failure modes may include system errors or user resistance, which could jeopardize the transition. The next action is to establish a clear timeline for the transition, including milestones for user training and system testing to ensure a smooth rollout.

The same-day reconciliation rule for cash variance surprises requires that any discrepancies identified must be addressed and reconciled within the same business day. The owner of this process should be the Treasury Operations Manager, who will trigger the reconciliation process upon identifying a variance. Evidence of compliance will include daily reconciliation reports and documentation of corrective actions taken. Failure modes may arise from delays in reporting or inadequate communication between departments, leading to unresolved discrepancies. The next action is to implement a standardized reporting protocol that ensures all variances are flagged and addressed promptly, with clear accountability assigned to relevant team members.
